justice: The space is dominated by a very large paved vehicle area with parked cars and buses, while dedicated pedestrian space (sidewalks/crossings) is not visible, indicating an inequitable allocation of space across road users.

Rules and priority are unclear because there are no visible crosswalks, pedestrian priority markings, or separated corridors; this can disadvantage non-motorized users and creates perceived unfairness in how different users can move through the space.

Limited pedestrian-oriented infrastructure (no sidewalks or shaded waiting areas visible) reduces usability for everyday social activity beyond vehicle access.

Tree/vegetation is set back to the perimeter with no integrated street trees or planted medians within the paved area, limiting carbon sequestration and microclimate benefits on-site.

bikeability: No bike lanes, cycle tracks, or shared-lane markings are visible; cyclists would likely need to mix with vehicles in an open parking/staging environment.
